question.worked_solution:
The domain of $y=\sqrt{x}$ is

$$
x\ge 0.
$$

To find the domain of $f(x)=5\sqrt{4x-3},$ we replace $x$ with $4x-3$ in the above inequality. This gives

$$
4x-3\ge 0.
$$

Solving this inequality, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-3 & \ge 0 \\ 4x & \ge 3 \\ x & \ge \frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain of $y=f(x)$ is $x\in [\frac{3}{4},\infty ).$

We can also see that this is true from the graph of the function. The graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown below.
